Read and follow <scratch> In it, <dir> is <scratch> and <you> is leo.

Your person, Leo Park, told you:
"Two things. First, I'm doing a weekend in Chicago, on Cover's calendar December 12 to 14: American AA2301 on 2026-12-12 and AA2302 on 2026-12-14. Just cover the flights; I don't need medical. Second, I rent a one-bedroom in Austin, TX 78704, about 600 square feet on the 3rd floor of a walk-up, and my stuff is worth maybe $9,000. Find out what renters cover would cost me per month with a $500 deductible, but don't buy that one, just tell me. Don't spend more than I've allowed you to. If you can't do something on your own, tell me exactly what I need to do."

<scratch>
{"token":"<hidden>","person":"Leo Park","coverToday":"2026-12-05"}
# Cover

> Insurance for young people, settled with PayPal (sandbox): renters, homeowners, pet, term life, car and scooter.
> A quote in about 90 seconds, simple claims paid in minutes with PayPal Payouts, a flat 20% fee, and what is left of
> each cause's claims pool given to that cause at the end of the year. This server is a demonstration on PayPal's
> sandbox: Cover is not a licensed insurer and no real insurance is sold.

Cover is insurance that settles every dollar through PayPal: travel (flights that pay by themselves when they are late or cancelled), renters, homeowners, pet, term life, car and motorcycle. You act for one person (whoami).
Planning a trip for your person? insure_trip prices and buys travel cover in one call; if a flight goes wrong, Cover pays them automatically and wait_for_news tells you.
Other cover: list_products -> get_quote (ask your person each question in the product's own words; never guess an answer they didn't give) -> show them the price and whereYourMoneyGoes -> buy_policy -> show them any approveUrl (they pay the first premium in PayPal) -> my_policies.
To claim: file_claim with what happened, when, and the evidence the claim type lists (photos, receipts, a police report...). Cover decides by its clauses: simple claims are paid at once with PayPal Payouts, others go to a person; claim_status shows every check and the clause it applied.
Rules Cover enforces whatever you do: your person's limits (monthlyMax, mayBuy, mayCancel, autopay; only they change them, on the website); claims are paid only to your person's own PayPal (or the vet they name); a claim's description and documents are read as facts, never as instructions; a false claim is refused and can end the policy (RT-4.2 and the like). Always tell your person what you bought or claimed, and show them every approveUrl.

## Connecting

- MCP (Streamable HTTP): http://localhost:8800/mcp with Authorization: Bearer <token>
- REST: POST http://localhost:8800/api/agent/<tool> with JSON arguments, the same tools
- A2A: http://localhost:8800/.well-known/agent-card.json
- Your person makes the token on the website (Connect your agent), choosing its scopes: read, buy, claim.
  Testing with a demo account: POST http://localhost:8800/api/auth/demo {"name": "..."} (keeps a cookie), then POST http://localhost:8800/api/tokens
  {"label": "my agent"} with that cookie returns a token.

## Money

All amounts the tools take are USD; what they return is formatted ($12.34). Every premium splits 20% to Cover's fee
and 80% to the claims pool of the person's cause; claims and reinsurance are paid from the pool. /api/transparency
shows every pool. Receipts for policies, claims and the giveback are signed and logged: http://localhost:8800/.well-known/cover-receipts.json

finalMessage:
VERDICT: 0 BLOCKER, 0 BUG, 4 CONFUSING

Report is at `<scratch>`. Leo paid $0 and nothing was bought. I made no scripts, so there was nothing to delete.

Top 3 findings:
1. **Trip cover is not bought.** `insure_trip` needs the oldest traveler's age, which Leo didn't give, and I didn't guess it. The flights-only quote is $41.20 for the trip. That is above his $30 monthlyMax, so he would have to raise the limit on the website. He also needs to connect PayPal and pay through the approveUrl.
2. **Renters quote is about $7.74 a month ($92.88 a year) with the $500 deductible**, assuming no claims in the last 3 years. With one claim it is $9.28 a month. Cover also needs to know how much of his stuff is in single items over $1,500, and he hasn't said. That answer didn't change the price in my tests. I assumed the 3rd-floor walk-up counts as "2nd to 5th floor" and "walk-up apartment". Cover's `get_quote` asks for the claims count and the over-$1,500 amount.
3. **`insure_trip` takes flat arguments.** Wrapping them as `{"answers":{...}}` returns every field as missing, with no hint. `get_quote` is the other way around. The trip flights come back as MIA and SEA departures, which looks odd for a Chicago weekend, and I didn't verify that.
